A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Goldilocks benchmark work, retaining Hadrian, Eclipse, and corresponding experiments. Text, tables, and figures are readable. V1's supplementary material on pages 13–26 was inspected; v2 ends with references and contains no appendix. The substantial revision supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original train/test overlap measurements, controlled training comparisons, benchmark evaluations, and domain-shift and cross-fold ablations in Sections 3–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of Hadrian, Eclipse, and Twins-IND, additional benchmark comparisons, and domain, fold-overlap, and demographic analyses in Tables 2–5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The Hadrian/Eclipse construction procedures and recognition architectures are retained. V2 Section 3.4 adds a Twins-IND-specific curation procedure: constrain genuine pairs by pose or acquisition environment, exclude profile images from impostor candidates, and select difficult candidates using similarity. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 adds Twins-IND, introducing identical-twin verification with pose and indoor/outdoor variation. Figure 6 adds recognition evaluations on SLLFW, DoppelVer, MLFW, XQLFW, and TALFW beyond v1's performance comparisons. The established training datasets remain. V2 Table 5's female Hadrian labels contradict its male-only construction description, so they do not reliably establish expanded Hadrian population coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and retained ablation comparisons use the same five recognition methods: ArcFace, CurricularFace, MagFace, AdaFace, and UniFace. V2 extends this method set to additional benchmarks without adding or replacing recognition baselines. Newly cited synthetic-face methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: V1's equal-size ID-Disjoint, ID-Overlap-R, and ID-Overlap-C training-control experiment is removed. V2 introduces Twins-IND's 6,000-pair evaluation design, including an 85%/15% demographic composition and an exception allowing one identity across nine folds, and adds demographic-stratified evaluation. The retained Hadrian/Eclipse pair counts, ten-fold accuracy protocol, and ResNet100 backbone remain as reported.

E4.justification: V1's train/test overlap audit, cleaning controls, and supporting duplicate-image/identity galleries are removed. V2 extends the fold-overlap ablation to Twins-IND, adds demographic accuracy breakdowns and observations about unrestricted hard-sample repetition, and expands demographic composition analysis while dropping the gender chart. The random-MORPH domain control is retained with identical scores, moving from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 3.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean ten-fold accuracy without repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or formal significance tests. V2's additional averages and result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds Twins-IND results averaging 71.57%, additional benchmark comparisons, and demographic results, while removing v1's train/test overlap results. Shared entries also change: MS1MV2/ResNet100 ArcFace scores on Hadrian and Eclipse change from 91.45% and 81.27% in v1 Table 4 to 91.48% and 81.17% in v2 Table 2. These are reported value changes; the PDFs do not establish their cause.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. V2's added average-accuracy and accuracy-difference rows summarize empirical results rather than introduce new mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion shift from demonstrating train/test leakage bias and introducing two benchmarks to introducing three benchmarks for natural attribute variation and similar-looking identities. Comparability with artificially degraded-image benchmarks becomes central. Existing repetition, demographic, and fold constraints are elevated into an explicit contribution; fold-disjointness remains a claim.

C2.justification: V2 newly argues that easy doppelganger benchmarks underrepresent twin-recognition difficulty and that natural attribute variation can rival artificial degradation. It acknowledges Twins-IND's demographic imbalance and imperfect fold separation, plus generalizability concerns from 6,000-pair test sets. V1's explanations of label cleaning amplifying train/test-overlap bias disappear; the domain-shift and cross-fold interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses img2pose alignment, FairFace's coarse classes and identity-level majority voting, and free data redistribution subject to identification and an agreement. Conversely, it removes v1's named selection checkpoint and shared implementation details covering RGB inputs, augmentation, flipped-feature summation, squared Euclidean scoring, and Partial-FC. The platform reference becomes an anonymous placeholder, although the main dataset link remains. Newly disclosed preprocessing does not establish an actual preprocessing change.

R1.justification: The literature review drops its duplicate-image/identity-overlap discussion and reframes the work around natural attributes, artificial degradation, and similar-looking identities. It adds positioning relative to SLLFW and synthetic-face research, including SynFace, DCFace, and Vec2Face, and proposes the benchmarks as tools for assessing synthetic datasets. This substantially changes research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, literature review, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Dataset construction becomes Section 3, benchmark positioning becomes a standalone Section 4, and the numbered ablation subsections become discussion paragraphs alongside limitations and access conditions. Some supplementary material moves into the main narrative, and citations change to author–year style.

P2.justification: V2 removes the overlap violin plots and duplicate galleries, moves and expands the Hadrian rejection montage, and adds accepted-pair illustrations and a benchmark-accuracy plot. The demographic chart is expanded and redrawn. Tables gain Twins-IND entries, averages, differences, and demographic breakdowns; the statistics table replaces train-disjointness with fold-disjointness. Several figures and tables now use wrapped text layouts.

improvement.justification: Twins-IND and the additional benchmark comparisons broaden the paper's empirical usefulness, and v2 adds concrete limitations and access information. However, v1's shared implementation details disappear, weakening reproducibility, while v2 Table 5 reports female Hadrian groups despite Section 3.2 defining Hadrian entirely from male pairs. These unresolved consistency and documentation problems offset meaningful additions without supporting a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
